# RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 signatures made by OpenSSL 4.1.0 (openssl genpkey, openssl dgst -sign)
# over the 28-byte ASCII message "weaver-dnssec backend parity". A third library signs, so
# both backends are checked against signatures neither made.
# The lines from rsa1025-sha256 on were made the same way where they are ordinary signatures
# (rsa1025, rsa2047: openssl genpkey -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:1025 or 2047, openssl dgst
# -sha256 -sign). The rest are genuine for the key they name, computed in Python 3.15 from the
# private values that openssl rsa -text prints, over the EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 SHA-256 encoding EM:
#   e1: the rsa2048-sha256 modulus with e = 1, signature = EM.
#   digestinfo-*: the rsa2048-sha256 key, EM^d mod n over a malformed DigestInfo (no NULL
#     parameters; outer length in BER long form 81 31; two zero bytes after the digest).
#   e2, e65538, e2p32p1, e2p64p1: one new 2048-bit openssl key whose EM is a square mod p and q
#     and with gcd(32769, 2^32 + 1, 2^64 + 1; lambda) = 1. e2: a square root of EM by CRT.
#     e65538: that root to the power 32769^-1 mod lambda. e2p32p1, e2p64p1: EM^(e^-1 mod lambda).
#   modulus-even: n = 2 m, m the rsa2047 modulus; signature = CRT of EM^d mod m and EM mod 2.
#   Each satisfies signature^e mod n = its encoding: only a key or encoding check rejects it.
# Columns: label, hash, exponent (hex), modulus (hex), signature (hex), expected result.
